submission.summary:
Reviewed all 30 panel patients' medication lists; 6 were on apixaban. One (pt-1029, Margaret Allen) takes apixaban for acute pulmonary embolism, not NVAF, so it was out of scope and left unchanged. The other 5 have nonvalvular AF and were checked against the FDA label rule (2.5 mg BID if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL).

Changed (4):
- pt-1002 Linda Park: weight 57.6 kg + SCr 1.66 (9/18/26 nephrology letter, newer than the 1.18 on the flowsheet) = 2 criteria. 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID.
- pt-1008 Harold Bennett: age 81 + weight 128.3 lb (58.2 kg) recorded at the 9/24/26 visit = 2 criteria. The 9/28 pharmacy consult used a stale 5/2026 weight of 63.5 kg and concluded only 1 criterion. 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID.
- pt-1022 William Turner: only 1 criterion (SCr 1.61); age 79, weight 81.6 kg. Was inappropriately dose-reduced in 2024. 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID.
- pt-1028 Charles Young: age 82 + SCr 1.63 (9/15/26, risen from 1.31 at initiation) = 2 criteria. 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID.

No change (correct as written):
- pt-1019 Lisa Thompson: only weight 57.8 kg qualifies; SCr back to 0.86 after transient AKI; age 68. Continue 5 mg BID.

No other medications were altered.

Reviewed all 30 panel patients' medication lists; 6 were on apixaban. pt-1029 (Margaret Allen) was excluded because her apixaban is for acute PE (started 8/19/26), not NVAF, and 5 mg BID is correct for that indication. The other 5 have nonvalvular AF (echoes documented no significant valve disease) and were assessed against the FDA label criteria (2.5 mg BID if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL).

Changed (4):
- pt-1002 Linda Park: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Weight 57.6 kg (<=60) plus serum creatinine persistently >=1.5 (1.61 on 8/27/26 and 1.66 on 9/18/26 per the Lakeside Nephrology letter, CKD 3b with albuminuria) = 2 criteria. The in-chart 5/19/26 creatinine of 1.18 is outdated.
- pt-1008 Harold Bennett: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 81 plus current weight 128.3 lb (58.2 kg, <=60) documented at the 9/24/26 visit = 2 criteria. The 9/28/26 pharmacy consult recommending continuation used the stale 5/14/26 weight of 63.5 kg and missed the ongoing weight loss. SCr 1.31 does not meet.
- pt-1028 Charles Young: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 82 plus creatinine 1.63 (9/15/26) = 2 criteria; at initiation in 2/2025 only the age criterion was met, so the dose had not kept up with his renal decline.
- pt-1022 William Turner: 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID. Only 1 criterion met (creatinine 1.61); age 79 and weight 81.6 kg do not qualify. He was started on the reduced dose in 2024 for CKD/bleeding-risk reasons that are not label-supported, leaving him underdosed for stroke prevention. No bleeding documented (last review 9/12/26).

No change (1):
- pt-1019 Lisa Thompson: 5 mg BID is correct. Weight 57.8 kg is the only criterion met; the creatinine of 1.74 on 8/18/26 was transient AKI from volume depletion and has returned to 0.86 (9/2/26). Age 68.

No other medications were altered.

Panel-wide apixaban review (30 patients). Six patients were on apixaban; five had nonvalvular AF (pt-1002, pt-1008, pt-1019, pt-1022, pt-1028). pt-1029 was excluded because apixaban is for acute PE (8/2026), not AF; 5 mg BID maintenance is appropriate there.

Applied FDA label criterion (2.5 mg BID only if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL):

CHANGED (3):
- pt-1008 Harold Bennett: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 81 (meets) + weight 58.2 kg (128.3 lb measured at the 2026-09-24 visit, documented in the note but never entered on the flowsheet; the 9/28 pharmacy consult used the stale 63.5 kg value and concluded only 1 criterion). SCr 1.31 does not meet. 2 of 3 criteria -> dose reduction indicated.
- pt-1028 Charles Young: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 82 + SCr 1.63 (9/15/2026, CKD 3b, up from 1.31 at initiation). 2 of 3 criteria.
- pt-1022 William Turner: 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID. Only SCr 1.61 meets; age 79 and weight 81.6 kg do not. He was started on the reduced dose in 2024 for perceived bleeding risk, but this is subtherapeutic per label; no bleeding history, Hgb stable.

NO CHANGE (2):
- pt-1002 Linda Park: age 60, weight 57.6 kg (1 criterion), SCr 1.18 -> 5 mg BID correct. (Note: documented OTC naproxen use raises bleeding risk - worth clinician follow-up.)
- pt-1019 Lisa Thompson: age 68, weight 57.8 kg (1 criterion); SCr 0.86 at baseline after resolved AKI (transient 1.74 in Aug 2026) -> 5 mg BID correct.

Correction disclosure: while updating pt-1028 I initially submitted the change against the wrong medication id (med-1028-01, metformin), briefly setting metformin to 2.5 mg BID. I immediately restored metformin to its original 500 mg twice daily and then applied the apixaban change to med-1028-03. Final med list for pt-1028 verified correct: metformin 500 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, apixaban 2.5 mg BID. No other medications were altered.

Reconciled outpatient medication lists for the 4 patients discharged from Valley General on/after 9/17 (pt-1006, pt-1011, pt-1012, pt-1025). Each list was updated to reflect the discharge summary plus any post-discharge changes documented in the chart; inpatient-only and completed short-course drugs were not added.

pt-1006 (Thomas O'Brien, NSTEMI w/ LAD DES, d/c 9/22): increased metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg -> 50 mg daily; added pantoprazole 40 mg daily for GI protection on DAPT. Did NOT add clopidogrel (stopped 9/29 by Lakeside Cardiology for CYP2C19 *2/*2 poor metabolizer) and instead added ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily; did NOT add discharge lisinopril 5 mg (stopped 9/25 by Dr. Okafor for orthostatic lightheadedness/hypotension, never dispensed on list). Aspirin kept at 81 mg (no higher with ticagrelor), atorvastatin 80 mg and metformin unchanged.

pt-1011 (status migrainosus, d/c 9/28): added topiramate 25 mg at bedtime (continuing per 9/30 portal message despite paresthesias) and ondansetron 4 mg as needed; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN continued. IV inpatient agents not added.

pt-1012 (hypertensive urgency/hyponatremia/UTI, d/c 9/28): stopped lisinopril (ACEi cough) and started losartan — entered at 100 mg daily per Dr. Okafor's 9/30 titration from the discharge dose of 50 mg; stopped hydrochlorothiazide permanently (hyponatremia); converted metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID to metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; increased metformin to 1000 mg BID; added empagliflozin 10 mg daily (held 9/30 for cost, restarted 10/1 after copay assistance per telephone note). Home omeprazole 20 mg retained and inpatient pantoprazole not added (formulary substitution only). Cefpodoxime not added — 7-day course completed the evening of 9/30. Aspirin and atorvastatin unchanged.

pt-1025 (left leg cellulitis with AKI, d/c 9/23): reduced lisinopril 10 mg -> 5 mg daily per discharge; metformin and rosuvastatin resumed/unchanged. Cephalexin not added — course completed 9/29.

No changes were made to any other patient's chart. Note for the care team: discharge summaries recommend follow-up BMPs (pt-1012 around 10/5, already scheduled; pt-1025 at the 1-2 week PCP visit); I did not place lab orders as the request was limited to medication reconciliation.

pt-1012 (hypertensive urgency, hyponatremia, UTI): stopped lisinopril (ACE-inhibitor cough) and hydrochlorothiazide (hyponatremia, not to be restarted); stopped metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID and started metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; increased metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Kept home omeprazole 20 mg and did not add pantoprazole, which was only an inpatient formulary substitution. Aspirin and atorvastatin unchanged.

pt-1025 (cellulitis with AKI): reduced lisinopril 10 -> 5 mg daily per discharge; metformin and rosuvastatin resumed unchanged.

Note for the care team: follow-up labs are pending per the discharge instructions (BMP for pt-1012, already scheduled 10/5, and BMP for pt-1025 at the PCP visit); I did not place lab orders as the request was limited to medication reconciliation.
